purpose: The v8 skill inventory. Training data is built skill by skill with a coverage floor per skill; each run is judged per skill by v8/skillscore.py over v8/dev_skills.json. Example phrasings here were written for this file (a different world from the eval corpora) and MAY be used as training seeds.
judgement_note: judgement=true marks skills where asking back (the runtime's clarify, reached via `done` or a call over an ambiguous set) is an acceptable outcome.

groups.desc: Copying spans from the message into calls: names, anchor words, titles, numbers, dates.
Kind routing: the question's form decides which kind of row answers it.
Field filters on a set: open/overdue, field values, numeric comparisons, the trash.
Link walks from one row to its related rows.
Time windows, relative shifts, which date field a window applies to, ordering by time.
Number answers: count, sum, one row's amount, dtstart of, group balance, owed_*.
Follow-ups that refine, extend, switch or resume the conversation's current set.
Row handles: reading the #n shown, ordinals, rows from several turns back, `them` and multi-row.
One skill per write verb (verbs of one call shape share a skill).
Composing writes: look-then-write, bulk, `A then B`, corrections, undo.
Judgement: ask on real ambiguity, say nothing, refuse by reason.

skills.desc: Copy a proper name (person, place, group, album, trip) letter for letter into `called`/`search`; never respell, shorten or swap it for a similar word.

examples.say: find Omar Haddad
anything about Alfama in my notes?
show me the Garden 2026 album
which people share the House Bills group with me?
calls: answer (members of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

skills.desc: Pick the matching word(s) out of a descriptive phrase: the head noun(s) a row's title would carry, dropping my/the/thing/stuff, verbs and filler.

examples.say: what's the code for the gym locker?
find the note I made about the old boiler
where's my passport scan?
have I got anything on the vet?

skills.desc: Write a create's title / description / content from the message: drop the command words ('add a task to', 'remind me to', 'make a note to'), capitalise the first word, keep the person's own words and details.

examples.say: remind me to renew the car insurance
jot down a note: ask Lena about the lease
keep the bike lock combination 2291 in my locker
add a task to email the landlord about the heating
calls: schedule.add_task{title: "Email the landlord about the heating"}

skills.desc: Turn numbers said in words into digits: money into minor units (sixty dollars → 6000, twelve fifty → 1250), plain counts and minutes as they are (half an hour → 30, three photos → 3).

examples.say: log sixty dollars for the plumber in House Bills, I paid
who owes me more than thirty bucks?
which task is roughly a twenty minute job?
where have I taken exactly three pictures?

skills.desc: Copy a day or time into a write the way it was said ('thursday', 'the 3rd', 'next monday'), spoken times as 24h ('at two' → 14:00, 'half nine' → 09:30); leave the date out when none was said.

examples.say: monday I need to call the bank — add that as a task
put yoga on saturday at ten
coffee with Kofi tomorrow at 3pm
calls: schedule.propose_event{summary: "Coffee with Kofi", dtstart: tomorrow at 15:00}

examples.say: add a task to sort out the garage

skills.desc: 'Who …', a person to find, a surname, 'my <role>' (my plumber, the Lena from choir) → people rows (`parties`), never the events or debts that mention them.

examples.say: find Sofia Marin
what's Kofi's surname?
the Lena from choir — who is she exactly?
which contact is my plumber?

skills.desc: 'What's on X', 'what have I got that day', 'anything happening on …' → everything dated that day: `things during X` (calendar, open to-dos, birthdays), listed `ordered by dtstart asc`.
calls: answer (things during saturday) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: saturday — what's planned?
calls: answer (things during saturday) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: anything going on the 9th?
calls: answer (things during the 9th) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: what have I got tomorrow?
calls: answer (things during tomorrow) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: how does my thursday look?
calls: answer (things during thursday) ordered by dtstart asc

skills.desc: Pick the schedule kind the words name: calendar / appointment / 'what time is' / 'when do I' → `events`; list / to-do / due / tasks → `tasks`; birthday / anniversary → `important dates`.

examples.say: which appointments do I have next week?
when's Kofi's birthday?
what time's my vet visit?
what car tasks have I got?

skills.desc: Wifi, logins, passwords, PINs, codes, 'in my locker' → `locker items` (search does not reach the locker); the row, not the secret, unless the secret itself is asked for.

examples.say: what's the router login?
how many things have I got saved in the locker?
any gym entries in my locker?
what's the alarm code at the lake house?

skills.desc: Notes vs journal vs documents: notes / 'I wrote down' / notebook → `notes`; my journal / diary → `journal notes`; document / paperwork / agreement / policy / scan / folder → `documents`.

examples.say: find my notes on the lease
what did I put in my journal yesterday?
do I have a copy of the tenancy agreement?
any paperwork for the boiler?

skills.desc: Photos / pictures / shots → `photos`; album → `albums`; 'where was it taken', 'places in my photos' → `places`.

examples.say: find the photo of the red door
what albums have I got?
which places show up in my photos?
show me pictures from the lake house

skills.desc: Spending → `expenses` (rows for 'what did we spend on …', a sum for 'how much'); 'do I owe / does she owe me' → the debts `obligations of (party)`; a shared-expense group → `groups` and its expenses/members.

examples.say: list the grocery expenses in House Bills
is there money I owe Omar?
show me the House Bills expenses
which expenses are in the Lisbon group?

skills.desc: No kind named: 'what do I have about X' → every kind (`things called "X"`); 'find X' / 'where's my X' where X names one thing → that one row only (look, then `answer #n`).

examples.say: what have I got on the Lisbon trip?
find the fridge warranty
where's the lease?
anything about Kofi's wedding?

skills.desc: 'Left', 'still', 'to do', 'due', 'open', 'haven't done' → `status != "completed"`; 'overdue' → `due_at during before now and status != "completed"`.
calls: (tasks) that (due_at during before now and status != "completed")

examples.say: what haven't I done yet?
am I late on any tasks?
calls: answer (tasks) that (due_at during before now and status != "completed")

examples.say: which steps of the move plan are still open?
which car jobs haven't I done yet?

skills.desc: A field equals a value: flags (`favorite = true`, `starred = true`), filing (`folder = "Tax"`, `notebooks = "Garden"`), kind/type (`kind = "phone"`), empty fields (`due_at is null`), and 'not me' (`party_id is not me`).

examples.say: which photos are favourites?
list the documents filed in Tax
show me the Garden notebook's notes
which to-dos are undated?
calls: answer (tasks) that (due_at is null and status != "completed")

examples.say: who else is in the House Bills group?
calls: answer (members of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

skills.desc: Compare a number field (`amount_minor > 10000`, `owed_to_me_minor > 3000`, `effort_min = 20`) or count a link (`count of photos = 3`).

examples.say: which House Bills expenses were over a hundred dollars?
which task is about an hour's work?
places I've only got one photo from
only those above twenty bucks

skills.desc: 'Did I delete / bin X', 'is X in the trash' → trashed rows are hidden unless asked for: `(<kind> called "X") that (deleted_at is not null)`.
calls: show (tasks called "gutter") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: is the gutter task in the bin?
calls: show (tasks called "gutter") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: is the old lease in the trash?
calls: answer (documents called "lease") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: has the kitchen picture been deleted?
calls: answer (photos called "kitchen") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: which notes have I thrown away?

skills.desc: Who is at an event, who a debt or a photo is with → `parties of (#n)`; 'who's coming' leaves me out: `(parties of (#n)) that (party_id is not me)`.
calls: answer (parties of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

examples.say: who's invited to the barbecue?
calls: answer (parties of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

examples.say: who is that debt with?
who's in this photo?
which person is my accountant?

skills.desc: A person's own rows: `obligations of`, `contact channels of` (number, email), `important dates of`, `activities of` (calls, coffees), `events of`.

examples.say: what's Omar's email?
when's my next meeting with her?
what was my most recent contact with Kofi?
calls: answer first 1 of ((activities of (#1)) ordered by started_at desc)

examples.say: is Sofia in debt to me?

skills.desc: A shared-expense group's `expenses of`, `members of`, `settlements of`; an expense's `groups of`.
calls: answer (members of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

examples.say: what's gone into House Bills?
list the people in the Lisbon group
calls: answer (members of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)

examples.say: which group is the ferry ticket in?
has anyone settled up in House Bills?

skills.desc: Photos ↔ places ↔ albums ↔ people: `photos of` a place / album / person, `places of` / `albums of` a photo; `(albums) that (member of (#n))`.

examples.say: where did I shoot that one?
which album is it in?
have I got photos of Lena?
pictures from Alfama
open the Garden 2026 album

skills.desc: The steps of a task: `tasks of (#n)`; 'what's left on the X plan' → `(tasks of (#n)) that (status != "completed")`.

examples.say: what are the steps for the move?
which garden project steps remain?
which bits of the wedding prep are done?

skills.desc: Named days and periods as said: `today`, `tomorrow`, `friday`, `the 9th`, `this week`, `this weekend`, `last month`, `next 2 months`, `recently`; a named month → its date range.

examples.say: which events do I have this weekend?
what's scheduled for the 9th?
calls: answer (things during the 9th) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: photos from april
whose birthdays fall in the next two weeks?

skills.desc: Relative moves: 'an hour later' → `by: +1h`, 'half an hour earlier' → `by: -30m`, 'a day later' → `by: +1d`; 'in three days', 'next friday' as windows.

examples.say: bump the call back by an hour
make yoga half an hour earlier
push it back a day
what's on in three days?
calls: answer (things during in 3 days) ordered by dtstart asc

skills.desc: Which date a window applies to: the row's own date `(set) during W`, or a named field — `due_at` (due), `completed_at` (ticked off / finished), `spent_on` (money), `captured_at` (photos, journal).

examples.say: what did I finish yesterday?
which tasks fall due on monday?
what was my spending last week?
calls: answer sum amount_minor of (expenses that (spent_on during last week))

examples.say: photos I took last weekend

skills.desc: A window the person doesn't name but the vault dates ('while we're away', 'on the trip', 'during the conference'): read the dates of the rows that define it, then use an absolute range `2026-07-02..2026-07-06`.

examples.say: what else is going on during my Lisbon stay?
calls: answer (things during 2026-07-02..2026-07-06) ordered by dtstart asc

examples.say: count the pictures from the Lisbon trip
anything else on while the conference is on?
calls: answer (things during 2026-09-14..2026-09-16) ordered by dtstart asc

skills.desc: 'Last', 'latest', 'most recent', 'next', 'earliest' → order and take: `first 1 of ((…) ordered by captured_at desc)`; a day's schedule `ordered by dtstart asc`.
calls: first 1 of ((journal notes) ordered by captured_at desc)
first 1 of ((activities of (#1)) ordered by started_at desc)

examples.say: show my most recent journal entry
calls: answer first 1 of ((journal notes) ordered by captured_at desc)

examples.say: what's the latest activity logged with Omar?
calls: answer first 1 of ((activities of (#1)) ordered by started_at desc)

examples.say: what's my earliest thing tomorrow?
calls: answer first 1 of ((things during tomorrow) ordered by dtstart asc)

examples.say: my newest photo?
calls: answer first 1 of ((photos) ordered by captured_at desc)

skills.desc: 'How many' → `answer count of (<set>)`.

examples.say: how many notes are in the Garden notebook?
how many pictures are from last weekend?
calls: answer count of ((photos) that (captured_at during last weekend))

examples.say: how many tasks are overdue?
calls: answer count of ((tasks) that (due_at during before now and status != "completed"))

examples.say: how many of them are still open?

skills.desc: 'How much did we spend', 'total', 'what does that come to', 'altogether' → `answer sum amount_minor of (<set>)`; over people `sum owed_to_me_minor of (them)`.

examples.say: what's the House Bills total so far?
add those up for me
total spending for this month?
calls: answer sum amount_minor of (expenses that (spent_on during this month))

examples.say: how much is that altogether?

skills.desc: One row's number: 'what did X cost / come to', 'how much is the balance' → `answer amount_minor of (#n)`.

examples.say: how much were the ferry tickets?
how much is the vet bill?
how much was that one?
how much is left to pay on the garage bill?

skills.desc: 'When's my X thing' with no kind given, where X matches rows of several kinds → `answer dtstart of (things called "X")` so the runtime asks back; never pick one candidate yourself.

examples.say: the vet thing — when is it?
when's the bank business?
when's the passport thing again?

skills.desc: 'How much does X owe me in the group / for the trip' → `answer balance of (#member) in (#group)`; 'and Y?' asks the same number for Y.

examples.say: what's Kofi's Lisbon balance with me?
where do I stand with Omar in House Bills?
and Lena?

skills.desc: Personal debts on people: 'who owes me' → `(parties that (owed_to_me_minor > 0))`; 'who do I owe' → `owed_to_them_minor > 0`; 'how much do I owe her' → `owed_to_them_minor of (#n)`; 'how much does he owe me' → `owed_to_me_minor of (#n)`.

examples.say: anyone owe me cash?
who am I in debt to?
what's my debt to Sofia?

examples.ctx: who am I in debt to?
examples.say: and the amount?

skills.desc: Refine the previous answer: 'just the weekend ones' → `answer (them during this weekend)`; 'only the open ones' → `answer (them) that (…)`; 'of those, the X ones' → `answer (them) called "X"`.

examples.ctx: which events do I have next week?
examples.say: just the ones on monday
narrow that to anything about the car
only the ones over fifty

examples.ctx: which tasks fall due this week?
examples.say: which of those are still open?

skills.desc: 'What else' = the set the conversation is on minus the row just discussed: `answer (<set>) except (#n)`; 'what else have I got that day' still lists the whole day.

examples.say: what other shots are in there?
what sits alongside it in that folder?

examples.ctx: which locker entries mention the flat?
examples.say: anything else on that shelf?
anything besides that on thursday?
calls: answer (things during thursday) ordered by dtstart asc

skills.desc: Same subject, another kind: 'is there a document for it too?', 'and on my task list?', 'photos of any of them' → the new kind over the same name (`documents called "X"`) or over `them` (`photos of (them)`).

examples.ctx: open my notes on the lease
examples.say: any documents on it?

examples.ctx: is the gym renewal on my calendar?
examples.say: is it a task as well?
any photos with them in?
sorry, the Garden notebook, not the folder

skills.desc: Same question, new subject: 'what about Alfama?', 'and Kofi?', 'and last month?' → repeat the previous call shape with the new name or window.
calls: (same shape as the previous turn, new name/window)

examples.say: what about Porto?

examples.ctx: what's Kofi's Lisbon balance with me?
examples.say: and Lena?
and last month?
calls: answer sum amount_minor of (expenses that (spent_on during last month))

examples.ctx: the harbour picture — where's that from?
examples.say: same for the sunset picture?

skills.desc: 'Back to X —' resumes an earlier thread: reuse the #n and sets from those turns, not the detour's.

examples.say: ok, returning to those pictures: put the second in Garden 2026
returning to the debts — which of those two is at saturday's barbecue?
back to the folder — bin the old lease
going back to the locker: reveal the router password as well

skills.desc: Point at the row the words describe in what was just shown ('the wifi one', 'the one with Lena', 'that', 'it', 'her') by its `#n`; never retype a title you can point at.

examples.say: star the lease one
the picture with Lena — put it in the album
which person does that involve?
make it monday instead

skills.desc: 'The first / second / last one' → the #n at that position in the last list as printed.

examples.say: the second — mark it complete
shift the top one to thursday
delete the last one
what's the third one?

skills.desc: A row from several turns back ('her', 'that balance', 'the note from earlier') keeps its `#n` for the whole conversation: use it, don't search again.

examples.ctx: (four turns after the debt #3 was shown)
examples.say: clear that debt now
her phone number, again?

examples.ctx: (the parking note was #1, three turns ago)
examples.say: put printing that parking note on my list
put down that I phoned him

skills.desc: `them` = every row of the last result (also when more were found than printed); several named rows → `#2, #5`.

examples.say: what do those add up to?
both of those can go on friday
which albums are they in?
photos with any of those people?

skills.desc: 'Remind me to', 'add a task', 'put X on my list' → `schedule.add_task{title: "…", due_at: …}` (due_at only when a day was said).

examples.say: remind me to water the plants tomorrow
new task: call Omar back
put renewing my passport on the list for the 30th
ok then, put it on my to-do list instead

skills.desc: Something at a time on a day → a calendar event: `schedule.propose_event{summary: "…", dtstart: <day> at HH:MM}`.

examples.say: put a vet appointment on tuesday at four
lunch with Sofia friday at 1
calls: schedule.propose_event{summary: "Lunch with Sofia", dtstart: friday at 13:00}

examples.say: book in a call with the bank monday at 9:30
calls: schedule.propose_event{summary: "Call with the bank", dtstart: monday at 09:30}

skills.desc: 'Make a note to / note down' → `knowledge.create_note{title}`; 'save / keep X in my locker' → `locker.add_item{type: "note"|"login"|"card", title, content}`.

examples.say: note to self: check the gutters
note down that the plumber prefers texts
the garage code is 8812 — keep it in my locker

skills.desc: Move a task or event: `reschedule{to: <day or day at HH:MM>} on #n`, or by an offset `reschedule{by: +1h} on #n`.

examples.say: can it go to thursday instead?
move the call to monday at 10
yoga should start an hour later
both of them can move to next monday

skills.desc: Mark done or star: `complete{} on #n` (a task), `core.star_document{} on #n` (a document).

examples.say: mark it done
first one's done
star that document
I've done the tax return task

skills.desc: Delete by kind: `delete{}` (task, event, note), `cancel{}` (an event call-off), `core.trash_document{}`, `tally.delete_expense{}`, `people.trash_person{}`, `locker.trash_item{}`, `media.delete_asset{}` — each `on #n`.

examples.say: get rid of my old car note
bin the parking expense
remove Kofi Mensah from my contacts
trash the blurry photo
call off the vet appointment

skills.desc: Put a trashed row back: `restore{} on #n` (task, note, photo, person), `core.restore_document{}`, `media.restore_asset{}`; an expense comes back with `tally.undo_expense{} on #n`.

examples.say: undelete it
restore the gutter task
calls: show (tasks called "gutter") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: bring the lease back
undo that expense

skills.desc: Only when the secret itself is asked for ('show me the password', 'what's the PIN') → `locker.reveal_receipt{columns: "password"} on #n`.

examples.say: what's the password on it?
what's the actual password for the router one?
reveal the gym one too

skills.desc: `media.add_to_album{album_id: (#album)} on #photo` — the album is a `#n` too (find it first if unseen).

examples.say: add it to the Garden 2026 album
put the sunset one in Lisbon highlights
add both to that album

skills.desc: 'Log that I called / had coffee with / visited / messaged X' → `people.log_interaction{kind: "call"|"coffee"|"visit"|"message"} on #party`.

examples.say: I phoned Omar, log it
I had coffee with Lena — log it
note that I messaged Kofi

skills.desc: Pay off a personal debt → `people.settle_debt{} on #debt-or-party`; settle a group balance → `tally.settle_up{to_party: me, group_id: (#g), amount_minor: balance of (#m) in (#g)} on #m`.
calls: tally.settle_up{to_party: me, group_id: (#1), amount_minor: balance of (#3) in (#1)} on #3

examples.say: mark that debt paid
pay Sofia back
square my Lisbon balance with Kofi
calls: tally.settle_up{to_party: me, group_id: (#1), amount_minor: balance of (#3) in (#1)} on #3

skills.desc: Add a shared expense `tally.add_expense{description, amount_minor, paid_by: me, group_id: (#g)}`, or add a person to a group `tally.add_group_member{group_id: (#g)} on #p`.

examples.say: add thirty dollars for the taxi to the Lisbon group, I paid
add Lena Novak to House Bills
put a 120 dollar electricity bill in House Bills
calls: tally.add_expense{description: "Electricity bill", amount_minor: 12000, paid_by: me, group_id: (#1)}

skills.desc: When a write's target hasn't been shown, find it first (`search "…"` / `show (<kind>) called "…"`), then write on its `#n`; a group or album argument is a `#n` too.

examples.say: trash the old lease
record that I rang Omar Haddad
I paid twenty dollars for snacks — put it in the Lisbon group

skills.desc: One write names everything it applies to: `delete{} on #1, #4, #7`; 'settle up with everyone' → ONE `tally.settle_up{…, amount_minor: balance of (it) in (#g)} on #2, #3, #4`; never piecemeal across calls or turns.
calls: tally.settle_up{to_party: me, group_id: (#1), amount_minor: balance of (it) in (#1)} on #2, #3, #4

examples.say: clear out everything gym-related
square up with all the House Bills members
calls: show (members of (#1)) that (party_id is not me)
tally.settle_up{to_party: me, group_id: (#1), amount_minor: balance of (it) in (#1)} on #2, #3, #4

examples.say: move the renewal to monday, task and calendar entry alike

skills.desc: Two different changes in one message → `A then B`.

examples.say: move the call to thursday and the booking to friday
calls: reschedule{to: thursday} on #2 then reschedule{to: friday} on #3

examples.say: tick off the first and delete the second
star it, and put printing it on my list
calls: core.star_document{} on #1 then schedule.add_task{title: "Print the lease"}

skills.desc: 'Sorry, it was the other X' / 'no — that one's thursday' → the same write aimed at the right row (plus any new change it names); the first write stands — this is not an undo.

examples.ctx: I rang Lena Novak — log it
examples.say: wrong Lena — I meant the other one

examples.ctx: put the second task on friday
examples.say: no, that one belongs on tuesday — friday is for the booking
calls: reschedule{to: tuesday} on #4 then reschedule{to: friday} on #3

examples.ctx: add the harbour one to the album
examples.say: wrong photo — the sunset one

skills.desc: 'Scratch that', 'put it back', 'I didn't mean to' right after a write → undo it on the same row: `restore{} on #n`, `tally.undo_expense{} on #n`.

examples.say: hmm, no — undo that

examples.ctx: remove Kofi Mensah as a contact
examples.say: no, bring him back
oops, I didn't mean that

skills.desc: A vague target (several Omars, 'the group' when there are two, 'all my X stuff' spanning many kinds): make the call over the set exactly as said and let the runtime ask; after `ambiguous: …`, name the `#n` if the message decides, else `done`.

examples.say: pay Omar what I owe him
is that Lena from work or the other one?
put Kofi in the group
how much have I paid into the group?
calls: answer sum amount_minor of ((expenses of (groups)) that (paid_by = me))

skills.desc: A walk over a link the vault doesn't hold ('is there an event at that place?') comes back `ambiguous: no link …` → `done` (the runtime asks); when a who/what link is ambiguous but the starting row already answers, `answer #n` with that row.

examples.say: any calendar event at that spot?
is the photo's Omar the same person?
saturday's lunch — who's it with?

skills.desc: The target is only in the trash, or nowhere: a write → `nothing`; a read → the honest empty set or 0, never a near-miss row of another name or kind.

examples.say: trash my note on the old van
calls: show (notes called "van") that (deleted_at is not null)

examples.say: any document for Alfama?
total spent back in march?
calls: answer sum amount_minor of (expenses that (spent_on during 2026-03-01..2026-03-31))

skills.desc: 'Never mind', 'forget it', 'actually no', 'leave it' before anything was done → `nothing`.

examples.say: actually, don't bother
forget it
scrap that, I'll check later myself
nah, leave it

skills.desc: Anything the vault doesn't hold or can't do — weather, the web, booking or buying online, sending a text or email — → `refuse: out_of_ontology`.

examples.say: will it rain in Lisbon tomorrow?
order more printer ink
send Omar a message saying happy birthday
reserve a table at the Italian place for friday

skills.desc: Protect the vault: sending a secret out of it → `refuse: sealed_egress`; inventing a password or code → `refuse: fabricated_secret`; 'delete everything' → `refuse: unbounded_destruction`.

examples.say: message Kofi the garage code
dump all my passwords into a spreadsheet
make up a new router password for me
wipe everything in my vault
